findings.title: SETTLED readback does not correlate the ledger usage receipt with the protocol receipt and reports invented zero usage
findings.mechanism: qualified() obtains a valid budgets.readback state, but readback() checks only state/usage_state and the separate model-protocol-receipt. It never compares the retained model-usage-receipt receipt_id to descriptor.request_id or its exact usage payload to the NO_MODEL settlement. Line449 emits zero whenever usage_state is KNOWN, irrespective of charged_output_tokens/history. The independent general ledger permits valid nonzero usage, so its validation does not enforce this consumer's special NO_MODEL invariant.

steps: Reuse test_qualified_projection_reaches_cold_admission_without_model_reservation(protocol_mode=True) to create a valid SOURCE owner/UDS/cold receipt and normal SETTLED readback.

At the existing readback consumer, independently reseal the in-memory retained model-usage-receipt with output_tokens=1, leaving the cold protocol receipt at zero. The actual ledger reducer accepts it and reports charged_output_tokens=1.
Call the unmodified model_protocol.readback and validate_readback: both accept SETTLED/KNOWN/output_tokens=0 identical to the positive.
Restore the valid row, then independently change only usage.receipt_id to a fresh UUID and reseal. Readback again accepts the same success despite the identity mismatch.
Restore all original rows and verify the positive again. No PostgreSQL records were changed.
reproducer.observed: Both negatives ACCEPTED; output_tokens=0 and same_as_positive=true. The tokens mutation had ledger_charged_output_tokens=1.

findings.violated_requirement: Architecture5.2 durable receipt/accounting truth and D2 exact request-id/dispatch-correlated receipt; KNOWN zero is justified only by the matching cold acknowledgement, not by an arbitrary independent KNOWN ledger event.
findings.impact: The affected reader can certify a contradictory persisted settlement as exact NO_MODEL accounting, including after Stop/fresh-reader replay. The underlying ledger remains charged according to its own history; this reproduction does not demonstrate a refund, extra send, live inference, provider cost bypass, or an external ability to modify immutable DB rows.
findings.minimal_remedy: Before returning SETTLED, validate the existing usage history's exact protocol-specific terminal receipt against descriptor.request_id and the expected KNOWN/output_tokens=0/provider_receipt_ref=null/cost fields=null settlement. Reject mismatch, do not rewrite history or simply project it to zero. Preserve the valid receipt and UNKNOWN no-refund paths; add focused SOURCE negative controls at this real reader. No ledger rewrite or new schema/owner is needed.

findings.title: The referenced model-configuration-receipt is resolved but its semantic payload is not checked
findings.mechanism: readback() validates the duplicated model_admission object with accept_preflight and only verifies that configuration_receipt_ref resolves to an owned record. It discards the return value from store.get at431-433 and never compares the durable configuration receipt to configuration_payload(prepared.payload, accepted.source_configuration), unlike the existing producer's persist_configuration checks at model_dispatch.py483-503.

steps: Start from the same valid produced SOURCE SETTLED graph and positive readback.
Change only the retained configuration receipt's inference_authorized field from false to true and reseal its envelope.

Update the protocol receipt's configuration_receipt_ref to that exact newly resealed envelope and reseal the protocol receipt. All identity/ref/digest forms remain valid; the copied cold model_admission remains unchanged.
Call the unmodified readback and validate_readback: the contradictory receipt is accepted and returned accounting equals the original positive.
Restore both rows and verify the valid positive again.

findings.violated_requirement: Qualified immutable configuration/receipt readback in D1-D2: a ref and selfdigest are not semantic agreement with the producer or the accepted cold observation.
findings.impact: Receive-only replay reports a coherent successful protocol settlement despite a contradicted durable configuration record. It does not itself authorize inference and does not establish a remote write primitive; the demonstrated defect is missing semantic/provenance validation at the persistent-reader boundary.
findings.minimal_remedy: Capture the exact owned configuration receipt returned by store.get; validate its kind and compare its payload canonically to the existing configuration_payload derivation from the qualified prepared payload and accepted source_configuration. Keep the reader non-writing/receive-only and preserve historical records. Add a valid positive and this resealed contradiction at the same reader.

pg_oracle_review.nodes: Existing baseline plus nominal/stop_first/send_first; author reports four collected nodes, not execution
pg_oracle_review.source_assessment: The authored oracle can exercise the stated first-PG boundary after concrete fixes; no new harness is needed.
pg_oracle_review.positive_boundary: Lines628-651 use independent synchronous observer C to see correlated descriptor/dispatch/SENT before delegating actual writer.write; exact body/frame digests, bytes and admitted caps are compared. Actual producer code commits reserve separately; the C query itself selects descriptor and SENT, not a separately returned reservation envelope.
pg_oracle_review.stop_first: Actual T0 exits before reserved Event. Existing service._locked is held by Stop; sender waits on Instance. pg_blocking_pids plus the current query identify overlap. After Stop commit sender refuses; readback must be RELEASED/UNKNOWN with zero writes and history without SENT (lines680-735).
pg_oracle_review.send_first: A's actual backend PID is captured. Synthetic peer holds ACK after real write; Stop is observed waiting on A before ACK release, then both tasks join (lines683-707). This is actual lock overlap if executed, not just asyncio ordering.
pg_oracle_review.poststop_readback: Lines751-762 compare replay after Stop and a fresh engine/consumer. This is a new connection/consumer, not a process restart or installed-native proof.
